clue.text: Give a makeover to Merchant Navy flag, removing middle

indicators.note: the central letter of the nine-letter flag name is taken away, leaving the rest joined

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships

explanation.surface: Someone redesigns the Merchant Navy's flag by cutting out its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing middle' drops N, the fifth of the nine letters of RED ENSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign something is to give it a fresh look, which is what a makeover does.

clue.text: Some picture galleries fit for a monarch

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain art galleries are grand enough for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, befitting a king or queen.

clue.text: Stop measuring a Greek goddess

parts.note: the prefix de- undoes or stops an action, as in de-ice or defrost
to meter is to measure, as a gas meter measures supply

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt measurement of some quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'de-meter', to stop metering; the goddess of harvest hides in that made-up verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Olympian deity of grain and harvest in Greek myth.

clue.text: Dogmatic when distributing food in Palestine

indicators.note: distributing spreads things around, so the letters of these words are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is rigid in their views about how aid is handed out in Palestine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; 'distributing' rearranges FOOD IN PALESTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-opinionated person is stubbornly convinced of their own views, much as a dogmatic one is.

clue.text: Village shop military leaders damaged

parts.note: generals are senior army commanders
tore means ripped, so damaged

explanation.surface: Army chiefs have wrecked the local shop in a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A general store sells a wide range of everyday goods, typical of a small rural community.

clue.text: Don't get despondent — there's a lot of liquid in the vessel

indicators.note: in places the measure of liquid inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup is a vessel for drinking
a hin is an ancient Hebrew liquid measure of several litres, hence a sizeable amount

explanation.surface: Cheer up: the cup is well filled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of liquid' is a biblical Hebrew measure, an obscure crossword staple; 'in' sets it inside the drinking vessel, and the surface hides the cheerful phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin up is an encouraging phrase urging someone to stay cheerful rather than downcast.

clue.text: Painter showing economy with his brush work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An artist is thrifty with paint in his brushwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' and 'with' are links; 'work' rearranges ECONOMY plus HIS BRUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish artist famed for fantastical, crowded panels such as The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: Robinia cultivated in African capital

indicators.note: cultivated plants are worked and tended, so the letters of the tree name are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A robinia tree is grown in an African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinia is the false acacia, a tree, which suits the gardening sense of 'cultivated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Old TV comedy series gratifies old tax collectors

parts.note: to gratify someone is to please them
IR stands for the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A vintage sitcom delights the retired taxmen.
explanation.walkthrough: PLEASE SIR! was a British school sitcom of the late 1960s and early 1970s; the Inland Revenue was merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Please Sir! was a classic British television sitcom set in a London school.

clue.text: Taking a risk bringing showy jewellery to school

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
bling is flashy, ostentatious jewellery

explanation.surface: A pupil risks trouble by wearing flashy jewellery to class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a place of learning but is a group of whales, a GAM; 'bringing ... to' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling means staking something on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Extremely pleasant going around European city of culture

indicators.note: the very-nice pair wraps itself around the abbreviation for European

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, which means extremely
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A delightful place appears around a European capital of culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European city of culture' looks like the whole definition, but 'European' gives E, which 'going around' puts inside V NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice in Italy is famed for its art, architecture and festivals, a cultural centre of the first rank.

clue.text: Clearly rebelling with unexpected Pro-Lenin vote

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome is one not in the expected order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprise vote for Lenin signals open rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in open revolt is to be rising up publicly against authority.

clue.text: Stop holding ton of bricks on the outside

indicators.note: the toy bricks sit on the outside, wrapped around the abbreviation for ton

parts.note: Lego is a brand of plastic toy building bricks

explanation.surface: Release your grip on a heavy load of bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ton of bricks' reads as a phrase, but 'of' only links: T goes inside LEGO.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to release one's grip.

clue.text: Almost get excited about African National Congress men being hostile

indicators.note: about places the shortened word around the other pieces
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or excite
ANC is the abbreviation for the African National Congress, the South African party
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers, so men

explanation.surface: Members of the ANC are angrily stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the final E; 'about' wraps the trimmed verb around the party initials and other ranks, the forces' term for soldiers below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means bitterly resentful, which is a hostile attitude.

clue.text: What might be studied in collisions could make cyclists happier

definitions.text: What might be studied in collisions

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be formed into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some field of study might cheer up cyclists.
explanation.walkthrough: Collisions here are those of particles in accelerators such as the Large Hadron Collider, not road crashes, which the cyclists suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists smash subatomic matter together in accelerators and study the debris to learn about fundamental forces.

clue.text: Weapons Bush somehow found inside vehicles

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are found inside the word for the weapons

parts.note: pikes are long spears used by foot soldiers

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arms are discovered hidden in George Bush's cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests George Bush's arsenal; the anagram indicator scrambles the surname and 'found inside' tucks it into the spears.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-bikes are pedal bicycles, humble vehicles.

clue.text: Indian batsman breaking hearts in Auckland when one short

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters apart so they can be rearranged
short means a single letter is lacking from the rearranged fodder

parts.note: A is a letter meaning one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A cricketer devastates New Zealand fans in their own city when just shy of a milestone.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARTS IN AUCKLAND has one A too many; rearranging it with an A ('one') removed gives the answer, flagged by 'breaking' and 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachin Tendulkar is the celebrated cricketer from Mumbai, the leading run-scorer in Test history.

clue.text: Swiss girl getting a cup

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from Switzerland wins a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large goblet, especially one used for communion wine.

clue.text: Teases family with soft material

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone mocks their relatives with gentle fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is leather made from young goats, prized for its softness.

clue.text: Source of growing intelligence somewhere in Essex?

definitions.meaning: playfully, a plant on which minds might grow, as fruit grows on a branch
a market town in the English county of Essex, north-east of London

explanation.surface: A place in Essex is mocked as where clever people grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; the question mark marks the whimsical first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Braintree is an Essex town; split, its name suggests a tree that grows thinkers.

clue.text: Note Lady Gaga is not well

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: gaga means crazy or senile, so the letters of the word beside it go haywire

explanation.surface: A report says the singer Lady Gaga is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Gaga' looks like the pop star, but 'Gaga' scrambles LADY into ADLY; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly can mean in poor health, as in feeling badly, an informal sense of unwell.

clue.text: Queen's left New York City for a long time

indicators.note: the Queen's abbreviation has left, so those letters are taken out of the city name

parts.note: Yonkers is a city in the state of New York
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch departed New York ages ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York City' tempts NYC, but it means a city in New York state, YONKERS; 'Queen's left' removes ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is British slang for a very long period, as in 'not seen you in ages'.

clue.text: Models and artist finally get as much money as possible from returned paintings

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the assembled letters are read from the end to the start
finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words before it

parts.words: get as much money as possible from
parts.note: to milk someone is to extract every penny you can from them

explanation.surface: Models and an artist squeeze every penny from paintings sent back to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes S and T from Models and artist; STMILK is then read backwards by 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Works by the Viennese artist Gustav Klimt are known by his name, so his canvases are its plural.

clue.text: Abandoned supporting London mayoral candidate without sex appeal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first pieces surround the abbreviation

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
Ken Livingstone stood several times for Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Backing a would-be mayor who lacks charisma has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', which would delete sex appeal, but here it carries its old sense of outside, so the first two pieces surround the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means deserted or left behind.

clue.text: Stable one who may be itemised

definitions.meaning: a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, one half of a couple described as an item

explanation.definitionFit: Steady means firm and unwavering, and as a noun a regular romantic partner.

clue.text: Artwork and other things, things not getting started

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things

indicators.note: not getting started means the first letter is not there

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Art and assorted other items, some never begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting started' drops T from THINGS, leaving HINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from engraved metal plates, a form of art.
